Class CellIterator

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.tfx.CellIterator
All Implemented Interfaces:
Iterable<CellIterator.CellEntry>
public final class CellIterator extends Object implements Iterable<CellIterator.CellEntry>
An iterator over terminal cells within a rectangular area.

CellIterator provides efficient access to terminal cells in a Buffer within a specified rectangular region. It supports optional filtering via CellFilter to selectively process cells based on their properties.

For optimal performance, prefer forEachCell(java.util.function.BiConsumer) over iterator-based iteration when you don't need iterator combinators.

  • Method Details

    • forEachCell

      public void forEachCell(BiConsumer<Position,Cell> consumer)
      Applies a function to each cell in the iterator's area.

      This is the preferred method for iterating over cells when you don't need iterator combinators. It's significantly faster than using the Iterator interface because it avoids coordinate calculations.

      The function receives the cell's position and the cell itself. To modify the cell, use Buffer.set(Position, Cell).

      Parameters:
      consumer - A function that takes (Position, Cell) and processes each cell

    • forEachCellMutable

      @Deprecated public void forEachCellMutable(BiConsumer<Position, CellIterator.MutableCell> consumer)
      Deprecated.
      Use forEachCellMutable(CellMutator) instead for better performance
      Applies a function to each cell in the iterator's area, allowing mutation.

      This variant provides a mutable cell consumer that can modify cells directly. The consumer receives the position and a mutable cell reference.

      Parameters:
      consumer - A function that takes (Position, MutableCell) and processes each cell

    • forEachCellMutable

      public void forEachCellMutable(CellIterator.CellMutator mutator)
      Applies a function to each cell in the iterator's area, allowing mutation.

      This is the preferred method for mutating cells. It avoids object allocation by reusing a single MutableCell instance and passing primitive coordinates. The MutableCell is reset for each cell, so do not retain references to it.

      Parameters:
      mutator - A function that takes (x, y, MutableCell) and processes each cell
